MINISTERIAL ORDER N o 004/2021
RYO KU WA 12/02/2021 GOVERNING
THE USE OF SUBSTANCES THAT
DEPLETE THE OZONE LAYER OR
MAY CAUSE CLIMATE CHANGE
The Minister of Environment;
Pursuant to the Constitution of the Republic
of Rwanda of 2003 revised in 2015,
especially in Articles 121, 122 and 176;
Pursuant to Law n° 48/2018 of 13/08/2018
on environment, especially in Article 16;
Having reviewed Ministerial Order nº
006/2008 of 15/08/2008 regulating the
importation and exportation of ozone layer
depleting substances products and
equipment containing such substances;
After consideration and approval by the
Cabinet, in its meeting of 14/12/2020;
ORDERS:
6

Article One: Purpose of this Order
This Order governs the use of substances that
deplete the ozone layer or which are likely to
cause climate change.
Article 2: Scope of this Order
This Order applies to controlled substances
that deplete ozone layer or may cause climate
change, products and equipment that contain
or rely on controlled substances that are
listed in Annex to this Order.
Article 3: Definitions
In this Order, the following terms have the
following meanings:
1 º Authority: the authority in charge of
conservation of environment;
2 º controlled substances: ozone
depleting substances listed in Annex
to this Order, in items A, B, C and E
and hydrofluorocarbons (HFCs)
substances listed in Annex to this
Order, in item F, including their
7

isomers, whether alone or in a
mixture, and whether they are virgin,
recovered, recycled or reclaimed;
3 º ozone depleting substances: a
substance that brings about a
reduction in the ozone layer gas in
atmosphere;
4 º reclamation: the reprocessing of a
recovered controlled substance in
order to meet the equivalent
performance of a virgin substance,
taking into account its intended use;
5 º recovery: the collection and the
storage of controlled substances from
products or equipment or containers
during maintenance or servicing or
before disposal;
6 º recycling: a cleaning process of a
recovered controlled substance in
order to be re-used.
8

Article 4: Prohibited substances and
equipment
Except when authorised by the Authority, it
is prohibited to produce, import, export, use
or sell controlled substances, and equipment
or products that contain or rely on controlled
substances listed in Annex to this Order.
Article 5: Phased-out substances
It is prohibited to produce, import, export,
use or sell phased-out substances that deplete
the ozone layer or that may cause climate
change, including equipment or products that
contain or depend on controlled substances
as provided for by Montréal Protocol on
substances that deplete the ozone layer as
amended to date, ratified by Presidential
Order n⁰ 143/01 of 03/04/2017.
Article 6: Discharge of controlled
substances into the environment
It is prohibited to discharge controlled
substances into the environment.
9

Article 7: Compliance measures
Without prejudice to penalties provided in
accordance with relevant laws, a person who
contravenes provisions of Articles 4, 5 and 6
of this Order is required to:
1° destroy controlled or phased-out
substances and equipment at his or
her own costs; or
2° re-export them where applicable, at
his or her own costs.
Article 8: Requirements to import, export,
recover, maintain, repair, reclaim or to
recycle controlled substances
A person who intends to import, export,
recover, maintain, repair, reclaim or recycle
the controlled substances and related
equipment must seek authorisation from the
Authority.
Article 9: Application for authorisation
A person who applies for an authorisation to
import or export, recover, maintain, repair,
10

reclaim or of recycling controlled substances
and related equipment submits his or her
application in writing to the Authority.
The application referred to under Paragraph
One of this Article is done via internet.
The application file for an authorisation
includes:
1 º a filled application form provided by
the Authority, containing
identification of the applicant, the
origin of controlled substances and
equipment that contain those
substances;
2 º chemical parameters of the
controlled substances;
3 º a company registration certificate;
4 º a trade licence certificate.
Article 10: Notification of a decision taken
on the application
The Authority notifies the applicant of a
decision taken on the application for an
11

authorisation of importation, exportation,
recovery, maintenance, repair, reclamation
or recycling of controlled substances and
related equipment within thirty (30) days
from the date a complete application file was
received.
The Authority notifies the applicant of a
decision taken via internet.
Article 11: Validity of authorisation
The authorisation of importation,
exportation, recovery, maintenance, repair,
reclamation or recycling of controlled
substances and related equipment is valid for
a period not exceeding three (3) years, from
the date of issuance.
Article 12: Obligations of a holder of an
authorisation
The authorisation holder has the following
obligations:
1° to comply with the annual import
quotas allocation;
12

2° to submit to the Authority an annual
report of the total quantities imported
or exported for the previous year.
Article 13: Temporary suspension or
revocation of the authorisation
In case of violation of provisions of this
Order, the Authority may suspend the
authorisation of importation, exportation,
recovery, maintenance, repair, reclamation
or recycling of controlled substances and
related equipment.
The authorisation is revoked from the holder
due to the following reasons:
1 º failure to comply with the terms and
conditions of the authorisation;
2 º illegal importation of controlled
substances or equipment containing
those substances;
3 º when an authorisation was issued
based on false documents or fraud.
13

Article 14: Fixing annual import quotas
The Authority fixes, every year, the national
import quotas of controlled substances based
on the quantity imported or exported during
the previous year.
The quotas of imported or exported
controlled substances are fixed on decreasing
scale across years.
Article 15: Communication of annual
import quotas of controlled substance
The national import quota of controlled
substances for the following year is
communicated not later than October of each
year.
Article 16: Application for import quota
The application for annual import quota of
controlled substances for the following year
is submitted not later than 30 th November of
each year.
Application file of an authorised importer for
14

annual import quota must show the
management of controlled substances
imported during the previous year.
Article 17: Labelling
Imported or exported controlled substances
and equipment containing those substances
must bear a label or any other indication
showing their nature, percentage and a
caution indicating consequences of using
those substances. They must also be with a
certificate indicating their origin material
and safety data sheet.
Article 18: Management of controlled
substances
A person who intends to recover, maintain,
repair, reclaim or recycle controlled
substances and related equipment must
comply with relevant laws and regulations.
The Authority sets up guidelines governing
management of controlled substances.
15

Article 19: Reporting
Not later than January every year, a person
who imports or exports, recovers, maintains,
recycles or reclaims controlled substances
reports to the Authority the following:
1 º the quantities imported and exported
for the previous year;
2 º the quantities recovered, recycled,
reclaimed or destroyed for the
previous year.
The Authority determines the format of the
report.
A person who imports or exports, recovers,
maintains, recycles, reclaims or destroys
controlled substances keeps a copy of the
annual report for five (5) years, after
submission to the Authority.
Article 20: Inventory of controlled
substances
The Authority carries out, every year, an
inventory establishing the volumes of
16

imported and exported controlled
substances, products and equipment
containing those substances.
Article 21: Repealing provision
Ministerial Order nº 006/2008 of 15/08/2008
regulating the importation and exportation of
ozone layer depleting substances products
and equipment containing such substances
and all prior provisions contrary to this Order
are repealed.
Article 22: Commencement
This Order comes into force on the date of its
publication in the Official Gazette of the
Republic of Rwanda.
17

Kigali, 12/02/2021
(sé)
Dr MUJAWAMARIYA Jeanne d’Arc
